title: Multivariable Chain Rule, Directional Derivatives & Gradients

sections.heading: Multivariable Chain Rule, Directional Derivatives & Gradients Practice Exercises

questions.q: Consider the function \( z = f(x,y) = x^2 + y^2 \). Let \( x = 2t \) and \( y = 3t \). Use the Multivariable Chain Rule to find \( \frac{dz}{dt} \) when \( t=1 \).
questions.answer:
We are given \( z = f(x,y) = x^2 + y^2 \), with \( x = 2t \) and \( y = 3t \). We need to find \( \frac{dz}{dt} \) using the Multivariable Chain Rule: \( \frac{dz}{dt} = \frac{\partial z}{\partial x} \frac{dx}{dt} + \frac{\partial z}{\partial y} \frac{dy}{dt} \).

First, find the partial derivatives of \( z \) with respect to \( x \) and \( y \):
\( \frac{\partial z}{\partial x} = 2x \)
\( \frac{\partial z}{\partial y} = 2y \)

Next, find the derivatives of \( x \) and \( y \) with respect to \( t \):
\( \frac{dx}{dt} = 2 \)
\( \frac{dy}{dt} = 3 \)

Now, substitute these into the chain rule formula:
\( \frac{dz}{dt} = (2x)(2) + (2y)(3) = 4x + 6y \).

We are asked to find \( \frac{dz}{dt} \) when \( t=1 \). First, find the values of \( x \) and \( y \) when \( t=1 \):
\( x = 2(1) = 2 \)
\( y = 3(1) = 3 \)

Finally, substitute these values of \( x \) and \( y \) into the expression for \( \frac{dz}{dt} \):
\( \frac{dz}{dt} \bigg|_{t=1} = 4(2) + 6(3) = 8 + 18 = 26 \).

questions.q: Consider the vector field \( \mathbf{f}(x, y, z) = \langle 12x,\, 20y,\, 11z \rangle \) on \( \mathbb{R}^3 \). Determine the scalar divergence \( \nabla \cdot \mathbf{f} \).
questions.answer: The divergence is \( 12 + 20 + 11 = 43 \).

questions.q: For \( f(x,y)=8 x - 15 y \), find the maximum possible value of the directional derivative \( D_{\mathbf{u}}f \) at any point, over all unit vectors \( \mathbf{u} \).
questions.answer: \( \nabla f=(8,-15) \) everywhere. By Theorem 2.1, the maximum directional derivative equals \( \lVert\nabla f\rVert=\sqrt{(8)^2+(-15)^2}=17 \).
